It does *not* say queens cannot be on the same diagonal if they are separated by more than one row. It just says "Queens may not touch". Touching usually means adjacent cells (horizontally, vertically, diagonally).
"Queens in consecutive rows cannot occupy columns differing by 1." -> This handles vertical adjacency and diagonal adjacency for immediate neighbors.
"Queens separated by more than one row MAY share a long diagonal; this is not the ordinary chess N-queens diagonal rule." -> This clarifies that if I have queens at (1,1) and (3,3), they are not touching, so it's allowed. The standard N-queens rule forbids *any* two queens on the same diagonal. This puzzle relaxes that: only immediate neighbors (row difference 1) cannot be diagonally adjacent. Row difference > 1 is fine even if on the same diagonal.
